claim: BRAFV600E is found in 45% of papillary thyroid cancers (PTC).
source: A recurrent activating mutation in BRAF, BRAFV600E, is found in 45% of papillary thyroid cancers (PTC), the most common histologic subtype (Xing, 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xing, 2005

claim: Mutations in BRAF are associated with an increased risk of disease recurrence in papillary thyroid cancer patients.
source: Although patients with PTC may be cured with surgery and radioiodine treatment, mutations in BRAF are associated with an increased risk of disease recurrence (Xing et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xing et al., 2015

claim: Expression of BRAFV600E increases thyrocyte migration and invasion through induction of epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) in vitro.
source: Expression of BRAFV600E has been demonstrated to increase thyrocyte migration and invasion through induction of an epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) in vitro (Baquero et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Baquero et al., 2013

claim: Transgenic mouse models expressing BRAFV600E develop aggressive papillary thyroid carcinomas that progress to poorly differentiated cancers.
source: Transgenic mouse models demonstrate that expression of BRAFV600E leads to aggressive papillary thyroid carcinomas that progresses to poorly differentiated cancers and demonstrate a loss of sodium iodide symporter expression and a failure to concentrate iodine (Knauf et al., 2005, 2011; Chakravarty et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Knauf et al., 2005, 2011 and Chakravarty et al., 2011

claim: Many human BRAFV600E mutant PTCs are slow growing cancers that may be clinically stable for years.
source: Yet many human BRAFV600E mutant PTCs are slow growing cancers, that may be clinically stable for years, and identifying these tumors is a key clinical challenge (Haser et al., 2016a, 2016b).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haser et al., 2016a, 2016b

claim: At five days post-fertilization, control tg-TOM larvae formed distinct well-organized thyroid follicles composed of TdTomato+ thyrocytes surrounding colloid containing thyroid hormone.
source: At five days post-fertilization (dpf) control, tg-TOM larvae formed distinct well-organized thyroid follicles composed of TdTomato+ thyrocytes surrounding colloid containing thyroid hormone, positioned in the ventral aspect of the jaw (Figure 1B), as previously reported (Wendl et al., 2002; Opitz et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1B and citations to Wendl et al., 2002 and Opitz et al., 2013

claim: tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae exhibited profound defects in thyroid follicle morphogenesis, forming disorganized clusters of thyrocytes.
source: In contrast, tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae exhibited profound defects in thyroid follicle morphogenesis, forming disorganized clusters of thyrocytes (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1C

claim: tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae displayed a significant decrease in the number and size of T4+ follicles compared to tg-TOM larvae.
source: In contrast, tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae displayed a significant decrease in the number and size of T4+ follicles (Figure 1E–G).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1E-G

claim: Total thyrocyte number was comparable between tg-BRAFV600E-TOM and tg-TOM control larvae at 5 dpf.
source: Total thyrocyte number was comparable between tg-BRAFV600E-TOM and tg-TOM control larvae (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C

claim: BrdU-positive TdTomato-positive cell number was not significantly different between tg-BRAFV600E-TOM and tg-TOM control larvae.
source: BrdU-positive TdTomato-positive cell number was not significantly different between tg-BRAFV600E-TOM and tg-TOM control larvae (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–F

claim: The total area and volume encompassed by Td-Tomato positive thyroid cells was comparable between tg-BRAFV600E-TOM and control larvae.
source: Additionally, the total area and volume encompassed by Td-Tomato positive thyroid cells was comparable between tg-BRAFV600E-TOM and control larvae (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G and H

claim: Expression of BRAFV600E in follicular cells disrupts follicle integrity, resulting in decreased number and size of follicles without altering cell number.
source: These results reveal that expression of BRAFV600E in follicular cells disrupts follicle integrity, resulting in decreased number and size of follicles without altering cell number.
evidence: Inference drawn from multiple experimental observations including follicle counts, size measurements, and cell counts

claim: Treatment with either dabrafenib or selumetinib alone was not sufficient to restore normal thyroid morphogenesis in tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae.
source: Treatment with either dabrafenib or selumetinib alone was not sufficient to restore normal thyroid morphogenesis in tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from drug treatment studies

claim: Combined treatment with both dabrafenib and selumetinib restored normal thyroid follicular structure in tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae.
source: By contrast, combined treatment with both dabrafenib and selumetinib restored normal thyroid follicular structure (Figure 2B), T4 production (Figure 2C), and led to a significant increase in the number and size of follicles (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2B-E

claim: Combined inhibition of MEK and BRAFV600E activity is required to restore normal follicular architecture and thyroid hormone (T4) production in tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that combined inhibition of MEK and BRAFV600E activity is required to restore normal follicular architecture and thyroid hormone (T4) production in tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae.
evidence: Inference drawn from drug treatment experimental results

claim: TdTomato-positive cells accounted for 0.076% and 0.060% of the total cells sorted in tg-TOM and tg-BRAFV600E-TOM respectively.
source: TdTomato-positive cells accounted for 0.076% and 0.060% of the total cells sorted in tg-TOM and tg-BRAFV600E-TOM respectively (Figure 3A), further confirming that the absolute number of thyrocytes is comparable between control and BRAFV600E transgenic larvae.
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3A

claim: Gene expression analysis revealed significant, differential gene expression between sorted thyrocytes from tg-TOM and tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae.
source: Gene expression analysis revealed significant, differential gene expression between sorted thyrocytes from tg-TOM and tg-BRAFV600E-TOM larvae (Figure 3B and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3B

claim: TGF-β and EMT are the most highly differentially induced pathways in BRAFV600E expressing thyrocytes.
source: This analysis revealed TGF-β and EMT as the most highly differentially induced pathways in BRAFV600E expressing thyrocytes (Figure 3C–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3C-D

claim: Immunostaining of transgenic zebrafish larvae revealed a loss of E-cadherin staining in tg-BRAFV600E-TOM thyrocytes.
source: Immunostaining of transgenic zebrafish larvae revealed a loss of E-cadherin staining in tg-BRAFV600E-TOM thyrocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F

claim: There is a significant positive correlation between BRAFV600E-induced signature in zebrafish and human ERK signature genes.
source: We found a significant positive correlation with human ERK signature genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–E), consistent with the activation of a conserved program of gene activation with expression of oncogenic BRAF.
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-E and citation to Pratilas et al., 2009

claim: BRAFV600E expression in thyrocytes induces alterations in thyroid follicle morphogenesis that are accompanied by gene expression changes in TGF-β signaling consistent with EMT.
source: These results demonstrate that BRAFV600E expression in thyrocytes induces alterations in thyroid follicle morphogenesis that are accompanied by gene expression changes in TGF-β signaling consistent with EMT.
evidence: Inference drawn from multiple experimental observations including morphology and gene expression data

claim: Five mpf tg-BRAFV600E-TOM adult animals are characterized by thyroglobulin-positive masses invading adjacent gills and skeletal muscle.
source: Five mpf tg-BRAFV600E-TOM adult animals are characterized by thyroglobulin-positive masses invading adjacent gills and skeletal muscle, features that are not observed in age-matched wild-type tg-TOM animals (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: Supported by histopathology data shown in Figure 4C-D

claim: A marked increase in p-ERK was observed in thyroid tissue dissected from tg-BRAFV600E-TOM fish compared to control thyroid tissue from tg-TOM fish.
source: Consistent with constitutive activation of BRAFV600E, we observed a marked increase in p-ERK in thyroid tissue dissected from tg-BRAFV600E-TOM fish compared to control thyroid tissue from tg-TOM fish (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4E

claim: At 12 mpf, tg-BRAFV600E-TOM animals showed evidence of progressive disease and histologic and cytological features diagnostic of thyroid carcinoma.
source: We analyzed a second cohort of tg-BRAFV600E-TOM adult animals at 12 mpf and found evidence of progressive disease and histologic and cytological features diagnostic of thyroid carcinoma (Figure 5), including highly invasive carcinomas with thyrocytes invading skeletal muscle and soft tissue (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by histopathology data shown in Figure 5

claim: Multiple specific cytologic features of papillary thyroid carcinoma including nuclear grooves, crowded and overlapping nuclei, and elongated nuclei were observed in tg-BRAFV600E-TOM animals at 12 mpf.
source: We also observed multiple specific cytologic features of papillary thyroid carcinoma including nuclear grooves, crowded and overlapping nuclei, and elongated nuclei (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by histopathology data shown in Figure 5C

claim: A desmoplastic stromal reaction was observed in 2/14 animals (14%) at 12 mpf.
source: Other features consistent with aggressive thyroid carcinoma including a desmoplastic stromal reaction (2/14 animals, 14%) were observed (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by histopathology data shown in Figure 5C

claim: Persistent expression of BRAFV600E in thyrocytes leads to invasive carcinoma with hallmarks of human PTC in 9/14 animals (64%) at one year.
source: These data reveal that persistent expression of BRAFV600E in thyrocytes leads to invasive carcinoma with hallmarks of human PTC in 9/14 animals (64%) at one year.
evidence: Supported by histopathology data from 12 mpf animals

claim: Transcriptomic analysis revealed significant, differential gene expression between normal thyroid tissue isolated from tg-TOM zebrafish and carcinomas isolated from tg-BRAFV600E-TOM animals at 12 mpf.
source: Transcriptomic analysis revealed significant, differential gene expression between normal thyroid tissue isolated from tg-TOM zebrafish and carcinomas isolated from tg-BRAFV600E-TOM animals (Figure 6B and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6B

claim: In adult thyroid carcinoma, there is persistent upregulation in TGF-β signaling, EMT, and glycolysis gene signatures.
source: As observed in thyrocytes isolated from larvae, we found persistent upregulation in TGF-β signaling, EMT, and glycolysis gene signatures from thyroid carcinomas isolated from 12 mpf zebrafish (Figure 6C, highlighted in red).
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 6C

claim: In adult thyroid carcinoma, the top upregulated gene expression signatures are linked to proliferation and metabolism (MYC, and mTORC1 gene sets).
source: However, in adult thyroid carcinoma we found that the top upregulated gene expression signatures are linked to proliferation and metabolism (MYC, and mTORC1 gene sets, highlighted in green).
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 6C

claim: Prolonged expression of BRAFV600E leads to upregulation of gene expression pathways associated with proliferation and regulation of cellular metabolism.
source: These results indicate that prolonged expression of BRAFV600E leads to upregulation of gene expression pathways associated with proliferation and regulation of cellular metabolism.
evidence: Inference drawn from GSEA analysis of adult thyroid carcinomas

claim: A gene signature of 58 genes identified in zebrafish thyroid carcinomas stratifies disease-free survival in human patients with papillary thyroid cancer.
source: We find that the gene signature identified in zebrafish stratifies disease-free survival in human patients and identifies patients at significantly lower risk of relapse (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by Kaplan-Meier analysis shown in Figure 6E using TCGA data

claim: Thyroid carcinomas arising in zebrafish are representative of slow growing, relatively indolent BRAFV600E-driven PTCs arising in human patients.
source: These data imply that thyroid carcinomas arising in zebrafish are representative of slow growing, relatively indolent BRAFV600E-driven PTCs arising in human patients.
evidence: Inference drawn from survival analysis correlating zebrafish gene signature with human patient outcomes

claim: The key transcriptional regulators of EMT, TWIST2 and SNAI2, are highly correlated with BRAFV600E signature genes in human PTCs.
source: We find that the key transcriptional regulators of EMT, TWIST2 and SNAI2, are highly correlated with BRAFV600E signature genes (Figure 7A, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by in silico screen results shown in Figure 7A

claim: Twist3, an orthologue of TWIST2, was significantly upregulated in BRAFV600E expressing thyrocytes.
source: We confirmed that Twist3, an orthologue of TWIST2, was significantly upregulated in BRAFV600E expressing thyrocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by qPCR validation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: Twist transcription factors are upregulated in thyrocytes after BRAFV600E expression and may be responsible for inducing broad gene expression changes linked to disruption of thyroid follicles.
source: These data indicate that Twist transcription factors are upregulated in thyrocytes after BRAFV600E expression and may be responsible for inducing broad gene expression changes linked to disruption of thyroid follicles.
evidence: Inference drawn from gene expression and correlation analyses

claim: Microinjection of a twist3 targeted sgRNA in combination with recombinant Cas9 protein leads to specific indels in the twist3 gene at the target locus.
source: Microinjection of a twist3 targeted sgRNA in combination with recombinant Cas9 protein leads to specific indels in the twist3 gene at the target locus, a majority of which are predicted to disrupt protein coding (Figure 7B).
evidence: Supported by CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing data shown in Figure 7B

claim: After microinjection of sgRNA targeting twist3, rescue of follicle structure and thyroid hormone production was observed in 57/173 (32.9%) tg-BRAFV600E-TOM embryos.
source: After microinjection of sgRNA targeting twist3, we observed rescue of follicle structure and thyroid hormone production in 57/173 (32.9%) embryos (Figure 7C–D).
evidence: Supported by CRISPR/Cas9 rescue experiment data shown in Figure 7C-D

claim: Non-targeting sgRNA-injected tg-BRAFV600E-TOM embryos exhibit profound defects in follicle structure and thyroid hormone production.
source: In contrast, non-targeting sgRNA-injected tg-BRAFV600E-TOM embryos exhibit profound defects in follicle structure and thyroid hormone production (Figure 7C) as previously described.
evidence: Supported by control experiment data shown in Figure 7C

claim: A deletion in the twist3 gene was identified in 1/12 clones (8.3%) from TOM+ cells isolated from embryos injected with a twist3 targeting sgRNA.
source: We identified a deletion in the twist3 gene in 1/12 clones (8.3%) from TOM+ cells isolated from embryos injected with a twist3 targeting sgRNA, and 0/12 clones isolated from TOM+ cells from embryos injected with a non-targeting sgRNA.
evidence: Supported by clonal analysis of FACS-sorted cells

claim: Genetic disruption of twist3 is sufficient to partially rescue the effects of BRAFV600E on thyroid follicle structure and hormone production.
source: These data indicate that genetic disruption of twist3 is sufficient to partially rescue the effects of BRAFV600E on thyroid follicle structure and hormone production.
evidence: Inference drawn from CRISPR/Cas9 rescue experiments

claim: Expression of BRAFV600E leads to significant disruption of follicle structure and thyroid hormone production without affecting proliferation in larval development.
source: By following thyrocytes from the earliest stages of specification, we are able to examine the timeline of oncogenic BRAFV600E in vivo where we observe significant disruption of follicle structure and thyroid hormone production. However, thyrocyte number remains normal in larval development.
evidence: Inference drawn from multiple experimental observations

claim: RNAseq analysis from sorted thyrocytes confirms that genes associated with EMT and TGF-β are transcriptionally activated by BRAFV600E.
source: RNAseq analysis from sorted thyrocytes confirms that genes associated with EMT and TGF-β are transcriptionally activated by BRAFV600E.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data and GSEA analysis

claim: BRAFV600E activation of downstream signaling pathways converges on a gene expression program that results in loss of epithelial organization without affecting proliferation.
source: These data suggest that BRAFV600E activation of downstream signaling pathways converges on a gene expression program that results in loss of epithelial organization without affecting proliferation.
evidence: Inference drawn from gene expression and proliferation data

claim: Pharmacologic inhibition of BRAF/MEK suppresses the morphologic alterations and restores normal thyroid follicle structure.
source: Pharmacologic inhibition of BRAF/MEK suppresses the morphologic alterations and restores normal thyroid follicle structure.
evidence: Supported by drug treatment experimental data

claim: Prolonged expression of oncogenic BRAFV600E leads to slow growing thyroid carcinoma with nuclear features similar to human PTC and gene expression changes conserved in human PTCs and predictive of improved disease free survival.
source: Prolonged expression of oncogenic BRAFV600E leads to slow growing thyroid carcinoma with nuclear features similar to human PTC and gene expression changes conserved in human PTCs and predictive of improved disease free survival.
evidence: Inference drawn from histopathology and gene expression analyses

claim: Expression of BRAFV600E leads to a disruption of follicle structure and thyroid hormone synthesis in zebrafish.
source: Expression of BRAFV600E leads to a disruption of follicle structure and thyroid hormone synthesis in zebrafish.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations in transgenic zebrafish

claim: Expression of BRAFV600E in rat thyrocytes demonstrated increased invasion and expression of markers consistent with EMT.
source: Our findings are consistent with prior studies performed in cell culture using rat thyrocytes that demonstrated increased invasion and expression of markers consistent with EMT after expression of BRAFV600E (Riesco-Eizaguirre et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Riesco-Eizaguirre et al., 2009

claim: In a mouse model of PTC, expression of BRAFV600E led to the development of poorly differentiated carcinomas associated with activation of EMT.
source: In a mouse model of PTC expression of BRAFV600E led to the development of poorly differentiated carcinomas associated with activation of EMT (Knauf et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Knauf et al., 2011

claim: Expression of BRAFV600E in human thyroid cancer cell lines induces SNAIL, represses E-CADHERIN, and leads to increased invasion.
source: Studies in human thyroid cancer cell lines in vitro also demonstrate that expression of BRAFV600E induces SNAIL, represses E-CADHERIN, and leads to increased invasion (Baquero et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Baquero et al., 2013

claim: Gene expression studies of human papillary thyroid cancer have identified increased expression of key EMT effectors in the invasive front of tumors.
source: Gene expression studies of human papillary thyroid cancer have identified increased expression of key EMT effectors in the invasive front of tumors (Vasko et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Vasko et al., 2007

claim: BRAFV600E has been found to physically interact and activate p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1), a serine/threonine kinase involved in promoting migration in human thyroid cancer cell lines.
source: BRAFV600E has been found to physically interact and activate p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1), a serine/threonine kinase involved in promoting migration in human thyroid cancer cell lines (McCarty et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to McCarty et al., 2014

claim: Epithelial organization and thyroid hormone production is disrupted in vivo after expression of BRAFV600E.
source: Our data significantly extend these studies and reveal that epithelial organization and thyroid hormone production is disrupted in vivo after expression of BRAFV600E.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from transgenic zebrafish

claim: The zebrafish model develops relatively slow growing thyroid cancer similar to the majority of human patients with PTC that grow slowly over many years.
source: In contrast to a transgenic mouse models that develops aggressive poorly-differentiated thyroid carcinomas, our zebrafish model develops relatively slow growing thyroid cancer similar to the majority of human patients with PTC that grow slowly over many years.
evidence: Inference drawn from comparison of zebrafish model with mouse models and human disease

claim: In a BRAF-mutant ATC mouse model, the combination of PLX4720 and PD0325901 was more potent in suppressing MAPK activation than either agent alone.
source: Similarly, in a BRAF-mutant ATC mouse model, the combination of PLX4720, a BRAF inhibitor and PD0325901, a MAPK kinase inhibitor, was more potent in suppressing MAPK activation than either agent alone (McFadden et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to McFadden et al., 2014

claim: Clinical studies with BRAF and MEK inhibitors in BRAFV600E-mutant melanomas confirm that combined therapy has greater anti-tumor efficacy in human patients.
source: Clinical studies with these agents in BRAFV600E-mutant melanomas also confirm that combined therapy has greater anti-tumor efficacy in human patients (Long et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Long et al., 2014

claim: Combined therapy with BRAF and MEK inhibitors may be required for treatment of BRAFV600E mutant thyroid carcinoma.
source: Our findings lead us to speculate that combined therapy with BRAF and MEK inhibitors may be required for treatment of BRAFV600E mutant thyroid carcinoma.
evidence: Speculation based on experimental findings in zebrafish and clinical data from other cancers

claim: Prolonged expression of BRAFV600E leads to an invasive thyroid carcinoma with diagnostic features of human papillary thyroid carcinoma in adult zebrafish.
source: Prolonged expression of BRAFV600E leads to an invasive thyroid carcinoma with diagnostic features of human papillary thyroid carcinoma in adult zebrafish.
evidence: Supported by histopathology data from adult zebrafish

claim: Gene expression studies from tumors isolated from adult animals reveal signatures of proliferation and alterations in mTOR signaling during progression.
source: Gene expression studies from tumors isolated from adult animals reveal signatures of proliferation and alterations in mTOR signaling during progression.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq and GSEA analysis of adult tumors

claim: In a mouse model of thyroid cancer, genetic inactivation of TSH receptor attenuated tumor initiation suggesting that TSHR signaling cooperates with oncogenic BRAF.
source: In a mouse model of thyroid cancer genetic inactivation of TSH receptor attenuated tumor initiation suggesting that TSHR signaling cooperates with oncogenic BRAF (Franco et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Franco et al., 2011

claim: Zebrafish thyroid carcinomas may arise slowly due to a relative euthyroid state that does not provoke elevated TSH levels.
source: We suggest that zebrafish thyroid carcinomas may arise slowly due to a relative euthyroid state that does not provoke elevated TSH levels, as seen in mouse models.
evidence: Speculation based on comparison with mouse models

claim: Additional genetic alterations may be required for development of carcinoma in zebrafish.
source: Alternatively, it is possible that additional genetic alterations may be required for development of carcinoma.
evidence: Speculation about mechanisms of tumor development

claim: Thyroid cancers in zebrafish exhibit similar histologic features to human papillary thyroid cancer.
source: Thyroid cancers in zebrafish exhibit similar histologic features to human papillary thyroid cancer.
evidence: Supported by histopathology data

claim: Key diagnostic features of PTC, such as nuclear grooves and elongation, are observed in zebrafish thyroid cancers, indicating conservation of these phenotypes across broad evolutionary distance.
source: Key diagnostic features of PTC, such as nuclear grooves and elongation, are observed, indicating conservation of these phenotypes across broad evolutionary distance.
evidence: Inference drawn from histopathology observations

claim: Tumor formation in zebrafish thyroid occurs on a tp53 wild-type background.
source: Interestingly tumor formation in zebrafish thyroid occurs on a tp53 wild-type background, in contrast to a zebrafish melanoma model in which tp53 loss of function is required for tumor formation (Patton et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by experimental design and citation to Patton et al., 2005

claim: Cellular context is important in modulating tumor initiation.
source: These results confirm the importance of cellular context in modulating tumor initiation, consistent with genetic studies from human patients, which demonstrate BRAF mutations in papillary microcarcinomas (Li et al., 2015), the earliest pathologic lesions identified.
evidence: Inference drawn from comparison of zebrafish and melanoma models, supported by citation to Li et al., 2015

claim: TWIST proteins are over-expressed in a significant fraction of thyroid cancers.
source: TWIST proteins are over-expressed in a significant fraction of thyroid cancers (Wang et al., 2013) and knockdown of TWIST1 in thyroid cancer cell lines led to a reduction in proliferation and migration (Salerno et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wang et al., 2013 and Salerno et al., 2011

claim: Knockdown of TWIST1 in thyroid cancer cell lines led to a reduction in proliferation and migration.
source: TWIST proteins are over-expressed in a significant fraction of thyroid cancers (Wang et al., 2013) and knockdown of TWIST1 in thyroid cancer cell lines led to a reduction in proliferation and migration (Salerno et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Salerno et al., 2011

claim: Genetic inactivation of twist3 suppressed the effects of oncogenic BRAFV600E in thyrocyte follicle structure and hormone synthesis.
source: Using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing we find that genetic inactivation of twist3 suppressed the effects of oncogenic BRAFV600E in thyrocyte follicle structure and hormone synthesis.
evidence: Supported by CRISPR/Cas9 experimental data

claim: These are the first in vivo data demonstrating a genetic requirement for TWIST expression downstream of BRAFV600E in a thyroid cancer model.
source: To our knowledge, these are the first in vivo data demonstrating a genetic requirement for TWIST expression downstream of BRAFV600E in a thyroid cancer model.
evidence: Claim about novelty of findings based on knowledge of existing literature

claim: Mutations in key signaling effectors of the mitogen activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway, including BRAF and RAS, are found in 70% of thyroid cancers.
source: Mutations in key signaling effectors of the mitogen activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway, including BRAF and RAS, are found in 70% of thyroid cancers.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about thyroid cancer genetics

claim: Papillary thyroid cancer is the most common histologic subtype of thyroid cancer.
source: A recurrent activating mutation in BRAF, BRAFV600E, is found in 45% of papillary thyroid cancers (PTC), the most common histologic subtype (Xing, 2005).
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge and citation to Xing, 2005

claim: Patients with PTC may be cured with surgery and radioiodine treatment.
source: Although patients with PTC may be cured with surgery and radioiodine treatment, mutations in BRAF are associated with an increased risk of disease recurrence (Xing et al., 2015).
evidence: Based on established clinical knowledge

claim: Identifying indolent thyroid tumors is a key clinical challenge.
source: Yet many human BRAFV600E mutant PTCs are slow growing cancers, that may be clinically stable for years, and identifying these tumors is a key clinical challenge (Haser et al., 2016a, 2016b).
evidence: Based on clinical knowledge and citation to Haser et al., 2016a, 2016b

claim: Current animal models largely recapitulate aggressive thyroid cancers.
source: While current animal models largely recapitulate aggressive thyroid cancers, there is a need to identify the molecular characteristics that differentiate indolent thyroid cancer from more aggressive subtypes and understand the molecular mechanisms that are involved in progression.
evidence: Based on knowledge of existing animal models

claim: There is a need to identify the molecular characteristics that differentiate indolent thyroid cancer from more aggressive subtypes.
source: While current animal models largely recapitulate aggressive thyroid cancers, there is a need to identify the molecular characteristics that differentiate indolent thyroid cancer from more aggressive subtypes and understand the molecular mechanisms that are involved in progression.
evidence: Statement about research needs in the field
